title: Say, Why Should Friendship Grieve for Those
description: Say, Why Should Friendship Grieve for Those in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 581 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Not lost, but gone before."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Say, why should friend-ship grieve for those Who safe ar-rive on Ca-naan's shore? Re-leased from all their hurt-ful foes, They are not lost but gone be-fore.

lines: Say, why should friendship grieve for those
Who safe arrive on Canaan's shore?
Released from all their hurtful foes,
They are not lost — but gone before.
How many painful days on earth
Now they enjoy a heavenly birth;
They are not lost — but gone before.
Dear is the spot where Christians sleep,
And sweet the strain which angels pour;
O why should we in anguish weep?
They are not lost — but gone before.
